harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restored the branch ledger on node1 and configured node2 as a persistent read-only MySQL replica. Replication, disconnect catch-up, read-only enforcement, and one-at-a-time reboot recovery all passed.
actions_performed: Installed CentOS 5-compatible MySQL 5.0.95 without changing the OS or kernel.
Preserved the staged ledger export and restored original rows 1001=12.50 and 1002=-3.25.
Configured node1 as the sole writable primary and node2 with read_only=1.
Verified normal committed inserts and disconnect/catch-up without missing or duplicate IDs.
Restarted node2 and node1 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.
Confirmed post-restart replication with final matching datasets: 6 rows, 6 unique IDs, total 40.00, zero lag.

evidence.requirement: Restore original ledger IDs and amounts while preserving the export
evidence.summary: Original rows were restored exactly, and the export retained checksum fcd54ac91dff5010c8dda0ddfa5cf2586d2d172456c7ca8ca33d0bffabc73700.

evidence.requirement: Use legacy-compatible software without changing OS or kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes use MySQL 5.0.95 from CentOS 5 repositories; node1 remains CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5.
The `repl_ledger` account is restricted to node2's IP; every listed privilege is N except Repl_slave_priv=Y.

evidence.requirement: Committed inserts on node1 arrive on node2
evidence.summary: Committed ID 1003 appeared on node2 at the matching executed binlog position with both threads running and zero lag.

evidence.requirement: Catch up after a short disconnect without loss or duplication
evidence.summary: Node2's I/O thread was stopped, IDs 1004 and 1005 were committed on node1 and remained absent while disconnected, then appeared after reconnection. Final count and distinct-ID count both equaled 5.

evidence.requirement: Node2 is read-only and node1 remains the sole application writer
evidence.summary: A non-super write on node2 failed with MySQL error 1290. Final state shows node1 read_only=0, node2 read_only=1, and matching data.
Healthy baseline and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, boot ID changed, and MySQL returned with intact data, read-only mode, both replication threads running, and zero lag.

Healthy baseline and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, boot ID changed, and MySQL returned with intact ledger data, export, replication account, and persisted firewall access for node2.
Post-restart committed ID 1006 replicated successfully. Both nodes contain the same six rows and total 40.00; node2 executed master position 312 with both threads Yes, zero lag, and no error.
